descriptions.Basophil: Characterized by coarse, intensely dark purple-black granules that cover the cytoplasm and typically obscure the segmented nucleus. Plays a major role in allergic responses and histamine release.
descriptions.Eosinophil: Distinctive bilobed nucleus with bright, refractive orange-pink/red cytoplasmic granules. Involved in allergic inflammation and defense against parasitic infections.
descriptions.Lymphocyte: High nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N:C) ratio with a compact, spherical dark purple nucleus and a narrow rim of light blue cytoplasm. Core mediator of adaptive immunity (T-cells, B-cells, NK-cells).
descriptions.Monocyte: Largest mononuclear leukocyte with a distinctive folded or kidney-shaped indented nucleus and abundant grayish-blue cytoplasm, frequently containing small vacuoles. Precursor to macrophages.
descriptions.Neutrophil: Polymorphonuclear leukocyte with a characteristic 3 to 5 lobed nucleus interconnected by fine chromatin filaments, surrounded by neutral pink-lilac cytoplasm with fine granules. Primary bacterial defense.
